C-FLUSH-AND-REPAIR.Summary:
Two deliverables: the flush of the staged record buffer under the D30 window, and the repair of the shipped expiring pins in the retirement suite. `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` holds exactly six entries, measured by the shipped `parseFrozenMarkdown` at this commit — findings `F221` through `F224`, all `###` headings, plus decision `D37`, a `##` heading, plus finding `F225`, staged between this spec's draft and this amendment — and no staged charter row (the shipped parse reports no registry heading and zero rows in either registry table — driven, not read). The flush set is exactly five of the six — `F221` through `F224` plus `D37`; `F225` is present and excluded, not this bundle's flush set (the findings genre has five lines of headroom after this flush and `F225`'s element is 34 lines, so it cannot land here; its own staged disposition defers it to the root-window bundle that pays `F216`). The flush renders the five into the record exactly as the shipped renderer shapes them: four `<Finding>` elements appended to live `findings.xml` after the last live element, one `<Decision>` element appended to live `rulings.xml` after the last live element, and five index `<Entry>` lines appended after the last existing entry in `decisions.xml`, ids `f221`, `f222`, `f223`, `f224`, `d37` in the delimiter-preserving slug form, with `layer="live"` and the genre each entry already carries in the buffer's own tokenizer. Bodies embed verbatim from the buffer — the buffer as it stands is measured flush-clean at this revision (zero raw `<` or `>`, zero bare `&` outside a staged escape, zero `[[f…]]`-form references, and the escape/decode round trip byte-identical for all six bodies, driven) — and no render-time normalization exists. The buffer itself is not this bundle's write scope and nothing here writes or prunes it: it is untracked and `.gitignore`d, so it has exactly one copy, and pruning the flushed entries is the authority's act after the flush PR merges, never a task here.
The second deliverable is measured, not assumed: the shipped `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY flush invariant` at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2285` pins fifteen ids `f206` through `f220` as `status="live"` (`:2299`, `:2307`) with their index `Entry` layers pinned to the same constant (`:2311`-2312), so the first legitimate payment of any pinned id — the record's payment queue opens at `F216` — reddens the shipped form on a record the shipped engine itself produced. This bundle rewrites the shipped assertion to the payment-invariant form — exactly once across the genre pair, status and index layer agreeing with the holding file, `f205`'s paid state kept as the durable pin — and writes its own new flush assertions in that same form, so this bundle adds no new pin (`AC-SUITE-PINS-REPAIRED`). The finding staged for this defect is `F225` in the buffer; it does not flush here (the findings genre's five lines of headroom after this flush cannot hold its 34-line element) and is paid by the root-window bundle that pays `F216`. `F225`'s staged disposition names this bundle by its pre-rename spelling; the buffer is the authority's file and this bundle repairs nothing in it.
The bundle pays nothing and retires nothing — measured, not assumed: the shipped payer map over both registry layers and the real archive mints 74 tokens and none of them is `F221` through `F225` or `D37`; no `PaidBy` is written, no row is minted, and the shipped validator reports zero findings on the post-flush record, so the close ceremony's own move reports `moved 0` and writes nothing (driven end to end on a throwaway copy of the repository at this commit). The set pinned by anchor id, never by position, is exactly `f221`, `f222`, `f223`, `f224`, `d37` — five entries flushed, four findings genre, one decision genre; the buffer's own header paragraph ("Holds six entries as of 2026-09-10") agrees with the shipped parse at this revision.
The constraint that decides whether this bundle is possible at all: every live genre root carries `base`, `headroom` and `ceiling` with `base + headroom = ceiling`, and `D28` forbids raising a ceiling — the shipped diagnostic says so in as many words (*"Raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy."*, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1545`). The roots are hand-written on every record write and only `--retire` rewrites them, which is `F216`'s recorded condition and this bundle's inheritance. Projected before any criterion was written and then driven, the post-flush roots read findings `base="7841" headroom="5" ceiling="7846"` — **five lines of margin**, the tightest a flush of this buffer's flush set can be — rulings `base="1776" headroom="107" ceiling="1883"`, index `base="276" headroom="20" ceiling="296"`, registry unchanged at `12 / 14 / 26`. The findings margin is thin enough that any prose added to an entry, any reflow, or any difference in wrapper shape breaches it, so every root figure below is bound to a read-back, never to a projection, and a read-back above a held ceiling is a stop-and-report, never a number to adopt. Binding live rulings `D28` (every genre carries a retirement rule and a size ratchet — the flush lands inside every persisted window), `D28.1` (eligibility is the enforcement and the ceiling the backstop; this bundle creates no eligible entry — measured), `D30` (scoped, not skirted — the record is this bundle's deliverable, so the freeze is scoped to the execution window that reads or rewrites the record files; no hard Constraint here transcribes a scalar count of any file it changes — the occupancy, margin and median figures live in Assumptions and expire), `D11` (nothing is deferred here; the guard question the buffer stages and the verb ruling it stages are recorded by the flush, not chartered by it — see NonGoals), `D27` (nothing is approved unread; ratification is the maintainer's). Name searched 2026-09-10 at this commit: no archive directory under `.ngrace/changes/archive/` or `docs/plans/archive/` and no `Row` in either registry layer carries `C-FLUSH-AND-REPAIR`; the name is new. The amendment renamed the bundle from `C-FLUSH-GUARD-AND-VERB`, whose words named work neither deliverable performs; the maintainer may veto the rename before ratifying.
C-FLUSH-AND-REPAIR.Problem:
The staged buffer is the authority's hold-out area under the D30 freeze: entries staged there are not in the record until a flush lands them. Six entries sit staged (`F221` through `F225` plus `D37`, measured by parsing the buffer with the shipped `parseFrozenMarkdown` at this commit — the shipped parser throws `split: missing anchor for heading at line N` on any adjacency defect, so a clean parse is itself the adjacency check); the flush set is exactly five of them, `F225` present and excluded. The flush is due now for a reason the ceiling arithmetic forces, and it is the last flush of its kind for a while:
**The findings genre is nearly out of room.** The live findings root reads `base="7673" headroom="173" ceiling="7846"` at this commit, and the four staged findings total 168 element lines by the shipped counting rule — leaving a margin of **5** against the held 7846. That is not a projection error to correct by trimming: the buffer is staged and frozen, its bodies are what they are, and `D28` forbids the alternative remedies (raising the ceiling is the shipped diagnostic's named non-remedy; trimming staged prose is a silent falsification of the record the buffer exists to hold). The flush fits — barely — and the criteria below bind the margin by read-back so that a one-line drift anywhere in the render stops the bundle loudly instead of sliding in.
**Nothing becomes eligible, so the window stays open.** A flush that minted a row or stamped a `PaidBy` would leave the committed tree holding an eligible element the validator refuses (`finding-eligible-still-live` / `registry-eligible-still-live` until a move runs). Measured at this commit: the payer map mints 74 tokens from registry rows in both layers and names none of the staged tokens, `D37` carries no `CodifiedIn`, and the post-flush validator returns zero findings — the committed tree is valid at every point of this bundle's life, with no mid-state the `D28.1` enforcement would flag.
**The buffer's entries name their own futures, and this bundle must not swallow them.** `F222`'s disposition queues the anti-occupancy guard's threat-model question as the first item of a follow-on queue, and `D37`'s Owner line sequences the `applied`/archive verb against that same queue — both name chartered bundles of their own, and both explicitly stay out of this one. The flush records them; it charters nothing.

Goals.Goal: The flush of exactly the anchors f221, f222, f223, f224 and d37 — selected by anchor id, matched as `` forms in the buffer, never by position. Four `` elements land in `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml` in the house shape the predecessors calibrated (open tag, `` carrying the heading line, `<Body>` carrying the buffer body, close tag — the shipped `renderFinding` shape at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:470`-478, which is not exported and is rendered to the same bytes by the flush), appended after the last live `Finding` and before the root close tag. One `<Decision>` element lands in `rulings.xml` the same way (the shipped `renderDecision` shape at `:480`-486). Five index `<Entry>` lines land in `decisions.xml` after the last existing entry, each ` <Entry id="…" token="…" genre="…" layer="live" />` — for the four findings, `genre="finding"`; for the decision, `genre="decision"` (derived from the existing index: `<Entry id="f220" token="F220" genre="finding" layer="live" />` beside `<Entry id="d36" token="D36" genre="decision" layer="live" />`). Bodies embed verbatim from the buffer — no render-time normalization exists, the buffer as it stands is measured flush-clean at this revision (zero raw `<`, zero bare `&` outside a staged escape, zero `[[f…]]`-form references, driven over all six bodies), and the five staged `<`-form escapes in `F221`'s body are preserved by the escape round trip: `xmlEscape` turns a staged `<` into the record's house `<` bytes, and the shipped decode returns the staged bytes — driven byte-identical for all six bodies. The citation rule this bundle adopts, the predecessor's: a citation that does not resolve does not enter the record — every fragment citation in the flushed bodies is measured resolvable against the index once the flush lands (sixteen `](#…)` citations across the five flushed bodies, destinations f204, f206, f25, f216, f220, f214 already indexed and f221, f222, f224, d37 landing in this same flush; the buffer's sixth entry carries three more citations that stay in the buffer with it; the citation validator exits 0 on the driven throwaway record), and any staged reference the gate would not resolve is a stop-and-report, never something to normalize away at render. The findings root is hand-written from a read-back, never from a projection: base equals the file's `newlineCount` after the write, headroom equals ceiling minus that base, and the ceiling stays 7846. The rulings and index roots are hand-written the same way against their held ceilings 1883 and 296. A read-back above a persisted ceiling stops the task and reports; it does not raise the ceiling, and it does not trim a staged body to make room.

The end state, driven rather than projected. After the flush the shipped validator exits 0 with zero findings on the production record, `--retire` reports `moved 0` and writes nothing (a byte-level no-op — the early return before any write, measured on the driven record), the preservation and citation validators exit 0, the shipped roots-invariant tripwire holds all four live roots, and `rulings-retired.xml`, `findings-retired.xml`, `registry.xml`, `registry-retired.xml`, `decisions.md` and `record-inventory.json` are byte-identical to this spec's base commit. Every value in the projections below was driven end to end on a throwaway copy of the repository with the shipped CLI and shipped functions at this commit, in a single pass over a pristine copy — the doubled numbers an earlier dirty-copy run produced were discarded as an artifact, never adopted. Anything else the validators report is a stop-and-report, not a number to adopt.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1 (module-change shape): the record the retirement validator governs, the retirement suite, and this bundle's own artifacts; no graph module is written, and exactly one `scripts/` file is edited (the suite: the production assertions the criteria name plus the shipped-pin repair `AC-SUITE-PINS-REPAIRED` charters — one file, both jobs). Roadmap: RM-GOVERNED-PATH (record integrity). Binding live rulings: `D28` (every genre carries a retirement rule and a size ratchet — the flush lands inside every persisted window, margins measured in Assumptions), `D28.1` (eligibility is the enforcement and the ceiling the backstop; the post-flush validator's zero findings is the enforcement silent), `D30` (scoped, not skirted — the record is this bundle's deliverable, so the freeze is scoped to the execution window that reads or rewrites the record files: no other dispatch touches the record while a record-writing task of this bundle is in flight, and no brief promises a frozen base across one; findings raised while this bundle is open go to `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` under the next staged number, never into the record under edit; no hard Constraint in this spec transcribes a scalar count of any file it changes — the occupancy, margin and median figures live in Assumptions and expire, and every criterion below asserts a relation its instrument can observe), `D11` (nothing deferred here lacks a dependency or a conflict), `D27` (nothing is approved unread; ratification is the maintainer's). The payment set is exactly empty: no token is paid by this bundle, and none can be — the payer map at this commit mints 74 tokens from registry rows in both layers and none of them is `F221` through `F225` or `D37` (measured with the shipped `derivePayerMap` over the real archive and both registry layers).

Order, ceiling, and CI. The committed sequence is: (1) the flush — findings first with the base read back, then `D37` into rulings with its base read back, then the five index `<Entry>` lines and the index base read back (the live-`Entry` rule, not lines); (2) validation exits 0; no `--retire` is run by this bundle — nothing is eligible after the flush (measured), so the close ceremony's own move reports `moved 0` and writes nothing, which is the F196 post-close rule this bundle inherits from the predecessor's measured shape. Do not raise the persisted ceiling. Do not mint a row. Do not write a `PaidBy`. A read-back above a held ceiling stops the task and reports; it does not raise the ceiling, does not trim a staged body, and does not reorder the flush to dodge the arithmetic — the honest outcomes are flush-as-specified or stop.

Buffer handling. The flush set is exactly the anchor ids f221, f222, f223, f224 and d37, matched as anchor forms in the buffer, never by position; the buffer as this amendment measures it holds six entries — the pinned five plus `F225` — and `F225` is present and excluded: it is not this bundle's flush set and stays in the buffer, and a further entry staged after this amendment is likewise not this bundle's flush set. Bodies embed verbatim: no render-time normalization exists — the buffer is measured flush-clean (six adjacent anchors, zero raw `<`, zero `[[f…]]`-form references, every raw `&` a staged escape's leading byte, and the `xmlEscape`/decode round trip byte-identical for all six bodies — driven at this commit), and any non-identity transform of a body byte is a deviation this spec's criteria refuse. The citation rule binds the same way: a staged cross-reference that would not resolve against the index does not enter the record — a stop-and-report, not something to normalize away at render. The staged entries' internal citations are already written in the delimiter-preserving slug form (`F9.1` is `f9.1`, never `f91` — the buffer's own staging convention, and the same rule this bundle's own artifacts obey); the flush must not repair them into any other form. Nothing in this bundle writes `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`: the buffer is untracked and `.gitignore`d, so it has exactly one copy and no backup, and pruning the flushed entries remains post-merge hygiene owned by the authority, not a task here. Because the buffer can be pruned at any moment after the flush PR merges, no close-bound criterion in this spec reads it: the verbatim-embed evidence is the flush task's read-back at execution time, while the buffer still holds the entries, and the close-time instruments assert only facts that survive pruning.

Write scope, anchors, and imports — enumerated once (F136.1's rule). Files this spec forces into write scope: the record files `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/findings.xml`, `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/rulings.xml`, `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.xml`; `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (the production assertions plus the shipped-pin repair `AC-SUITE-PINS-REPAIRED` charters, read-only over the record); and this bundle's own artifacts under `.ngrace/changes/active/C-FLUSH-AND-REPAIR/`. None of the record files carries a `LINKS:` header (checked at this commit; the `LINKS:` tokens inside them are prose in finding bodies, not file headers), the suite file carries none (checked at this commit), and no module in `.ngrace/graph/main.xml` owns any of them — the record and `scripts/` sit outside the graph's path set, and the lint config ignores `scripts/` (`.ngrace-lint.json` `ignoredDirs`). Do not mint a synthetic module, and do not repeat this list as a second module list anywhere. Do not register the record files in CONTEXT_ARTIFACTS. Do not add a lint issue code. Criterion mapping, stated plainly (the trap that has cost supersedes). Every `AC-*` below except `AC-NO-CURRENT-MODE` is close-bound by its own `CloseEvidence` child, and a task `Satisfies` that names any of them is the shipped error (`change.close-evidence-and-satisfied`, `src/lint/catalog.ts:286`). No criterion compares a fixed `git show` against a floating working-tree read (F215): every diff criterion's window is this bundle's own diff, stated in the criterion, probed in the post-close state, with this bundle's own archive directory excluded from archive pathspecs (F188) and tracked paths only (F174). Any test the later plan adds that measures the real repository carries an explicit generous timeout (F185). Task `Verification` and `TargetAssertions` contain no current-mode lint of this project root (F171 — the shipped detector misses the grace.ts form, so the check is by hand and is the one Satisfies-mapped criterion). Current-mode lint appears only as post-archive AC-CLOSE-LINT. The byte-invariance criteria here need no parse-based relaxation: none of the files they name is written by any shipped writer inside this bundle's window, because this bundle pays nothing and retires nothing (the zero-findings drive is the evidence) — `F221`'s structural-unchanged rule exists for files with multiple writers between an assertion's evaluation points, and no such writer touches these paths here.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Paying any token or minting any row. Owner: the tokens' own future charters; the record's payment audits. Measured at this commit: none of the six staged tokens appears in the payer map the shipped `derivePayerMap` derives over both registry layers (74 tokens, intersection empty), and this bundle mints no channel — no row, no `Pays` element, no `PaidBy` stamp — so the move reports `moved 0`, and a larger number is a stop, not an expectation.

Changing the record engine, the CLI, or any shipped constant: `parseFrozenMarkdown`, `renderFinding`, `renderDecision`, `persistSnapshot`, the eligibility scans, `checkCeilingValue`, the ceiling and provenance checks and `INDEX_HEADROOM_ENTRIES` already perform every operation this bundle needs — the shipped code needs no new change, and no `src/` file and no `scripts/` file other than the one suite file is edited. Writing or pruning `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md`, re-flushing any entry already in the record, or rendering any entry this spec does not pin. Owner: post-merge hygiene, the authority's. The buffer's entries beyond the pinned five — `F225`, staged between this spec's draft and this amendment, and anything staged after it — are the next flush's input, not this one's.

Raising any persisted ceiling, re-deriving any ceiling from the current base, hand-editing a `PaidBy`, or touching any genre's budget, constant, or diagnostic: the findings and rulings line budgets, the registry's live-row budget and headroom, the index's live-`Entry` budget and its clamp, and the rulings provenance ceiling — all shipped positions this bundle holds rather than revisits, and the shipped diagnostic's own words name the rejected remedy. AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FLUSH-LANDED:
After the flush, each flushed id — `f221`, `f222`, `f223`, `f224` as `<Finding>` elements, `d37` as a `<Decision>` element — exists exactly once across its genre's pair of files (`findings.xml` and `findings-retired.xml` for the findings; `rulings.xml` and `rulings-retired.xml` for `d37`), with no fixed expectation of which file holds it: the element's `status` agrees with the file that holds it (`live` in the live file, `retired` in the retired sibling), its token and genre agree, and the single `<Entry>` the index carries for the id has `layer` agreeing with that holding file — the relation survives the record's own payment cycle, which retires a finding, flips its index layer, and leaves every clause of the relation true. The house shape (open tag, `<Title>` carrying the heading line, `<Body>` carrying the buffer body, close tag), the append position (after the last live element of the live file, before the root close tag), and the verbatim body bytes are the flush task's read-back at execution time, while the buffer still holds them (the buffer is pruned post-merge by the authority, so no close-time instrument reads it, and no criterion here can depend on it). The written findings root base equals the file's `newlineCount` read back, headroom equals ceiling minus base, and the same read-back rule holds for the rulings and index roots. Content question. Failure: an element missing, duplicated across the pair, or carrying a disagreeing token, genre, or index `Entry` layer; an *unrepaired* ceiling raise — the read-back relations catch it; a base derived from a projection instead of the read-back; a render-time normalization applied silently. A ceiling raised with the relations repaired around it is not this criterion's red: that is the known boundary `AC-ROOTS-HELD` states. The instrument is the flush-invariant production assertion the later plan adds to `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (the C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 Goal-4 shape): the shipped parser walks the genre pairs and the index and requires exactly one matching element per flushed id with its `status` agreeing with the holding file, its index `Entry` layer agreeing with that status, and the agreeing token and genre — no fixed expectation of which file holds the element — plus the shipped `findingLineCounts` arithmetic for the read-back; the walk is the duplicate check. Shown green under payment — a driven throwaway copy where the shipped `--retire` moves one flushed finding to the retired sibling with its layer flipped consistently keeps the assertion green — and shown failing on mutated copies with a `<Finding>` element duplicated and with a flushed element's index layer flipped against its holding file (both driven).
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ROOTS-HELD:
The four live roots satisfy the shipped relations and no ceiling moved: for `findings.xml`, `registry.xml`, `decisions.xml` and `rulings.xml` — `base + headroom = ceiling` and each `base` equals its shipped metric read back (`newlineCount` for findings and rulings, the live-`Entry` rule for the index, the live `Row` count for registry), observed by the shipped roots-invariant tripwire (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`, the C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4 test at `:2023`). The relations are payment-invariant by construction: the only shipped writer of the roots, `persistSnapshot`, rewrites them in exactly this form under its clamp (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:958` — a ceiling holds or falls under the clamp, never rises), so the assertion holds across every later legitimate move. No `Entry` changes layer (this bundle's flush appends five live entries and flips nothing); no record file outside the three written files changes. Content question, answered by parsing the root lines. Failure: an observed relation broken on a mutated copy — a root whose `headroom` no longer sums against its ceiling, or whose `base` is derived from a projection instead of the read-back (both driven; the shipped tripwire reddens at `base + headroom = ceiling` and at `base equals its shipped metric read back` respectively). Known boundary, stated rather than hidden: a ceiling raised with these two relations repaired around it is not caught by any pin-free permanent instrument this bundle holds — the relations stay true, and the shipped validator refuses only `liveSize > ceiling` (`checkCeilingValue`, `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1514`), so a raised-and-repaired ceiling passes both the shipped validator and the shipped tripwire (driven). The equality-against-baseline instrument that would close that gap is the fixed-`git show` -against-a-floating-working-tree-read form this spec's own evidence-hygiene Constraint forbids (F215), so the boundary is not closed here; it is owned by the root-window bundle that pays `F216` — next in the record's payment queue, whose `--retire` re-derives the roots from the shipped formula and is the surface the gap belongs to. This criterion does not charter that bundle and does not adopt a raised ceiling for any root it reads.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SUITE-PINS-REPAIRED:
The shipped flush invariant in `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (`:2285`, the `C-FLUSH-AND-PAY flush invariant` shipped in PR #85) is rewritten to the payment-invariant form: it currently pins fifteen ids `f206` through `f220` as `status="live"` (`:2299`'s ternary, `:2307`'s status pin) and their index `Entry` layers to the same constant (`:2311`-2312), so the first legitimate payment of any pinned id — the queue opens at `F216`, whose owner names a later charter — reddens the shipped form on a record the shipped engine itself produced (driven: a throwaway copy where the shipped `--retire` moves `f216` to `findings-retired.xml` fails the shipped suite at exactly this test, 66 pass / 1 fail, `f216: expected status`). The rewritten assertion keeps what survives payment — each pinned id exists exactly once across `findings.xml` and `findings-retired.xml`, its `status` agrees with the holding file, its token matches, and its index `Entry` layer agrees with the holding file, with no fixed expectation of which file that is — and keeps `f205`'s assertion as a durable pin (a paid state is durable; a live one is not): `f205` retired, held by the retired file, index layer `retired`. The read-back arithmetic at the test's end stays. The same payment-invariant form is the shape of this bundle's new flush assertions (`AC-FLUSH-LANDED`), so the repair adds no new pin and the suite stops pinning any finding's liveness across a payment. Failure: the shipped form on a copy where a pinned finding has been paid — the shipped test reds and the repaired test on the identical state stays green (both driven); a mutation that duplicates a pinned element or disagrees an index layer still reddens the repaired form (the duplicate and layer-agreement checks are kept).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ELIGIBLE-NONE:
